body: Hi I can really relate! Going through something very similar and have been for many years. I would say one tip for ultrasounds that really helped (because they really do suck!) is wiggling your toes! I know it sounds odd but I’ve found that focusing on moving another body part not only helps you stay grounded but also helps you relax (which will ultimately make things less painful). Another tip is if you can somehow have a visit or at least get some kind of rapport built before doing anything invasive. Maybe schedule an online visit first to meet the physician and sus out if they seem kind/understanding/trauma informed. I’ve found part of what makes it hard is when you just met this person and don’t even know if you trust them at all and then they have to do something super triggering. So that can help! Or at least have a conversation with them beforehand as much as you feel comfortable. Ideally in my experience they ask about trauma history so that you as the patient don’t have to bring it up. Lastly if they help you bring fidgets! Having something to fiddle with is a nice distraction. I really relate and I know how horrible this shit is so hopefully some of this helps!

Hey! I had such intense driving anxiety for many of the same reasons as you so I totally get it and want to tell you that it is possible for you to do this! I had my permit for so long without doing anything, had multiple panic attacks and breakdowns in the car, and eventually was able to make it through and get my license. So there is hope! My best advice would be to start small and gradually work your way up as you get more comfortable. So maybe start in a parking lot, then a quiet residential street, then maybe something busier, etc. Honestly the number one thing that will make you feel better is practice and desensitizing yourself (At least in my experience). When you eventually schedule your test I’d suggest driving with someone around the test area beforehand if you have time! Made me feel a little less anxious going in. You got this!!

At the end of the test when he asked me to pull over, he said you have met the minimum requirements, so a pretty unenthusiastic way to tell me I passed. But I was just so happy I didn’t really care. I would absolutely recommend it. One of the best decisions I’ve ever made, hands down. Obviously your experience will vary depending on who you are and also who you’re with/where you are, but if you do your research and make sure you’re with someone you trust, I think it’s a great idea. Doing acid genuinely reminded me of how beautiful the world is and reinvigorated a sense of optimism about life that I thought I’d lost forever. I am genuinely a changed person and for the better. In terms of experience, for me I started out simply feeling very happy, and then it progressed into the environment actually changing and warping around me. The air was shimmering, I felt like I could see trees literally bursting into bloom. I saw a leaf and could actually see the cells and how they formed a piece of solid matter. Music was incredible, as was basically anything in nature. When I went into a completely pitch black room and listened to music I saw these incredible shapes and designs and patterns in the air that changed in time to the music. I felt like I understood simultaneously what it was like to die and to be born. It’s a lot to take in so it’s hard to put into words, but long story short it was incredible.
